A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Ca(2+) dissociation rates for the EF2 domain in S100B are slowed by 10-fold in the presence of the p52 peptide and that the Ca( 2+) binding affinity of the EF2 domain is enhanced by 10-fold by the p53 peptide.
the -Z position of the EF-hand is important for Ca(2+) binding and that the p53 peptide affects Ca(2+) affinity through its interaction with helix 3 of S100B.

(1) the -Z position of the EF2 domain is a critical residue for calcium binding in the EF-hand motif, (2) calcium binding to the EF-hand domain is a cooperative process, and (3) calcium binding in the presence of the p-53 peptide is more cooperative than calcium binding in the absence of the peptide.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Ca(2+) binding affinity of the EF2 domains is enhanced in the presence of the p 53 peptide, which may be due to a Ca(2+) induced structural rearrangement of the EF2 domain.
the -Z positions of EF-hand 1 and EF-hand 2 in S100B contribute to the calcium-binding affinity in a different manner, which is dependent on the presence or absence of the p53-derived peptide.
the Ca(2+) dissociation and association rate constants for the EF-hand mutants are not significantly affected when the target peptide derived from the p53 C terminus is present.
